en: around the end of the month

examples.en: I'm going to move around the end of this month.
I'll come visit you sometime around the end of the month.
My pay usually comes in around the end of the month.
It often snows around the end of December.
It's around the end of the month, so there's no moon in the night sky.

examples.ko: 그믐께에 맞춰 책을 다 읽으려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm trying to finish the book by around the end of the month.

explain: '그믐'에 '-께'가 붙어서 그믐 무렵을 말해요. 일상에서는 '월말쯤'이라고도 하고, 반대로 달의 중간쯤은 '보름께'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Are you free around the end of the month?
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '그믐께'보다 '월말쯤'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, '월말쯤' is used more often than '그믐께'.
phrases.en_equiv: around the end of the month

phrases.en: It looks like it will rain around the end of the month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 시기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add the particle '에' to mark the time.

phrases.en: Let's meet around the middle of the month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그믐께의 반대로 달의 중간쯤을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '그믐께', meaning around the middle of the month.

explain_en: '-께' is added to '그믐' to mean around the end of the month. In daily talk people also say '월말쯤', and the middle of the month is '보름께'.

examples.en: In the off-season, the villagers go on trips.

examples.ko: 저희 집은 요즘이 농한기라서 조금 한가해요.
examples.en: It's the off-season for farming at our house, so we're a bit free.
When the off-season comes, the country village gets quiet.
We decided to repair the house during the off-season.
Even in the off-season, greenhouse farming is busy.
The off-season usually comes in winter.

explain: 반대말은 농사일이 가장 바쁜 때를 가리키는 '농번기'예요. 가게나 일이 한가한 철은 '비수기'라고 하고, 농한기는 농사 이야기에서 써요.

phrases.example: 농한기를 보내면서 마을 사람들이 함께 책을 읽었어요.
phrases.en: During the off-season, the villagers read books together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 적은 철을 어떻게 지내는지 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for talking about how people spend the slow season.

phrases.example: 겨울이 되면 농한기가 돼서 일이 줄어요.
phrases.en: When winter comes, it becomes the off-season and there is less work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농사일이 줄어드는 철이 시작될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the slow farming season begins.

phrases.example: 농한기에는 마을 어르신들이 경로당에 많이 모이세요.
phrases.en: In the off-season, the village elders gather often at the senior center.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에는'을 붙여서 그 철에 하는 일을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '에는' lets you talk about what happens during that season.

explain_en: Its opposite is '농번기', the busiest farming season. For slow seasons in shops or other jobs people say '비수기', while 농한기 is used when talking about farming.

en: absence of holidays; absence of rest

examples.ko: 이 약국은 연중무휴라서 명절에도 문을 열어요.
examples.en: This pharmacy never closes, so it's open even on holidays.

examples.ko: 연중무휴라고 쓰여 있어서 일요일에 갔는데 문이 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: It said open all year round, so I went on Sunday, but it was closed.
The convenience store in my neighborhood operates every day of the year.

examples.ko: 연중무휴 식당이라서 언제든 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a restaurant that never closes, so you can go anytime.
It's reassuring that there's a hospital nearby open every day.

examples.ko: 연중무휴라는 말만 믿지 말고 전화해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't just trust the 'open every day' sign; try calling.

explain: 거의 항상 '연중무휴'로 가게 앞이나 광고에서 만나요. 반대로 쉬는 날은 '휴무'나 '정기 휴무'라고 해요. 그래도 명절이나 특별한 날에는 쉬기도 하니 가기 전에 확인하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: This restaurant is open all year round.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게가 쉬는 날 없이 연다는 광고에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in ads to say a shop never closes.

phrases.en: The mart operates all year without days off.
phrases.nuance_ko: '운영하다'와 함께 동사 문장으로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with '운영하다' to form a verb phrase.

phrases.en: This convenience store is open 24 hours a day, all year round.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밤낮없이 쉬는 날도 없이 문을 연다는 뜻으로 가게 앞에 자주 붙어 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on shop signs to say a place is open day and night with no days off.

explain_en: You almost always meet it as '연중무휴' (open all year) on shop signs and ads. The opposite idea is '휴무' or '정기 휴무' (regular closing day). Even so, some places still close on holidays or special days, so it's good to check before you go.

examples.en: The meeting date is still not confirmed.

examples.ko: 일정이 미확정이라 비행기 표를 못 샀어요.
examples.en: The schedule isn't confirmed, so I couldn't buy a plane ticket.

examples.ko: 미확정 소식은 말하지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to share unconfirmed news.

examples.ko: 출연자가 미확정 상태라서 방송 준비가 늦어요.
examples.en: The cast isn't finalized, so broadcast preparation is delayed.
If the place isn't settled, it's hard to book in advance.
It was reported that the pass result is still undecided.

explain: 반의어는 '확정'이에요. 일정이나 결과처럼 아직 정해지지 않은 것에 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '미정'이 있어요. '미확정 상태', '미확정이다'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The meeting place is still undecided.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미확정'과 비슷하지만 더 짧고 일상에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 미확정 but shorter and more common in daily use.

phrases.en: The result is still in an undetermined state.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 정해지지 않은 상황을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a situation that hasn't been settled yet.

phrases.en: I'll tell you right away when the schedule is confirmed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미확정'의 반대로, 정해졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 미확정: it has been decided.

explain_en: The opposite is '확정'. It is used for things like schedules and results that aren't settled yet, and '미정' is a similar word. It commonly appears as '미확정 상태' and '미확정이다'.

examples.en: It will take about an hour to get to the airport.

examples.ko: 소요된 비용은 나중에 돌려받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get back the money spent later.

examples.ko: 비자를 받는 데 보통 2주가 소요되는 편이에요.
examples.en: Getting a visa usually takes around two weeks.
The costs are running higher than expected.

examples.ko: 서류 심사에 시간이 소요돼서 많이 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: The document review took time, so it got delayed a lot.
How long does it take by taxi?

explain: '시간이 걸리다'와 같은 상황에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 공지나 안내문에서 '소요 시간', '소요 비용'처럼 자주 보여요. 친구와 말할 때는 '걸려요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: It takes about an hour to get to the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소요되다'와 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 소요되다 but far more natural in daily conversation.

phrases.example: 안내문에 소요 시간이 두 시간이라고 적혀 있어요.
phrases.en: The notice says the required time is two hours.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공지나 안내문에서 일이 걸리는 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to state how long something takes.

phrases.example: 여행 소요 비용이 얼마나 되는지 계산해 봤어요.
phrases.en: I calculated how much the trip would cost.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 드는 돈을 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to talk about the money a task requires.

explain_en: A formal counterpart of 시간이 걸리다. Signs and notices often show 소요 시간 (time needed) and 소요 비용 (cost needed). With friends, 걸려요 sounds much more natural.

t90.ax: How long does it take by taxi?

examples.en: Our school's autumn sports day is an annual event.

examples.ko: 이 축제는 해마다 열리는 연례행사가 됐어요.
examples.en: This festival has become an annual event held every year.
I'm going to the countryside for the yearly kimchi-making.
It's an annual event, so I cleared my schedule in advance.
I'd feel sorry if I missed the annual event.
Like a yearly ritual, we argue about the same thing every year.

explain: 해마다 때가 정해져 열리는 행사를 말해요. 매년 되풀이되는 일을 농담처럼 말할 때도 '또 연례행사네'라고 해요. 같은 말로 '해마다 하는 행사'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 가족 여행이 우리 집 연례행사가 됐어요.
phrases.en: The family trip has become an annual event in our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해마다 하는 일이 습관처럼 자리 잡았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something done every year has become a fixed habit.

phrases.en: We're making kimchi again this year. It's our annual event again!
phrases.nuance_ko: 해마다 되풀이되는 일을 농담처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking remark about something that happens every year.

phrases.example: 우리 마을에는 해마다 하는 행사가 있어요.
phrases.en: Our town has an event that is held every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연례행사'를 쉬운 말로 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way of saying 연례행사.

explain_en: It refers to an event held at a fixed time every year. People also joke about things that repeat every year by saying '또 연례행사네'. You can also spell it out as '해마다 하는 행사'.

examples.ko: 저희는 다음 주에 여행을 예정하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are planning a trip next week.
I scheduled the meeting for Friday.
I will set the show for three p.m.
They're a couple planning to marry next year.
I planned my vacation for August, so I bought a plane ticket.

examples.ko: 예정한 날짜를 바꿔야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think we have to change the planned date.

explain: 말할 때는 '계획하다'나 '~할 예정이에요'를 더 자주 써요. '예정하다'는 날짜와 시간이 정해진 일에 어울려서 공지, 뉴스에서 보여요. 막연한 생각에는 '생각 중이에요'를 써요.

phrases.en: I'm planning to move next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예정하다'보다 말할 때 훨씬 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more common in speech than '예정하다'.

phrases.en: Let's meet on the planned date.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 정한 날짜나 시간을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for a date or time already decided.

phrases.en: I'm planning a trip with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 날짜가 정해지지 않은 일에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but also works for things without a set date.

explain_en: In speech, '계획하다' and '~할 예정이에요' are used more. 예정하다 suits events with a set date or time and shows up in notices and news. For a vague idea, say '생각 중이에요' (I'm thinking about it).

dis.h: fix something for a set time
gh: make a general plan of steps
plan and organize a project or event
think up an idea in your head

p.n: 예정하다 sets a date or time for something; 계획하다 does not take a date like this naturally.

t90.ax: We are planning a trip next week.

en: to be decided; to be determined; to be finalized

examples.en: The schedule has not been finalized yet.
Our team's departure date has been confirmed.
I will tell you as soon as your acceptance is confirmed.
Please tell people only the finalized plan.
The day the exam results are finalized is Friday.

examples.ko: 가격이 확정돼서 포스터를 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: The price is settled, so we can make the poster.

explain: '정해지다'는 일상에서 아무 때나 쓰지만, '확정되다'는 바뀔 수 있던 일이 마지막으로 정해졌을 때 써요. 일정·가격·합격 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 아직 안 정해졌을 때는 '미정'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I will send you the finalized schedule by email.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 이상 바뀌지 않는 일정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a schedule that will no longer change.

phrases.en: Please let me know once the date is decided.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마지막으로 정해진 다음을 말하는 연결 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This connective form refers to the moment after something is finally settled.

phrases.en: That student's admission has been confirmed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합격 결과가 마지막으로 정해졌을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a common pairing for when a pass result is made final.

explain_en: '정해지다' is the everyday word, while '확정되다' is for something that could still change and has now been settled for good. It pairs well with schedules, prices, and acceptances. When something is not yet decided, people say '미정'.

dis.h: made final and confirmed, no more changes
gh: general word for something being decided
formal; decided by a group vote

p.n: 결정 only says it was decided; it doesn't stress that it is now final.

t90.ax: The schedule has not been finalized yet.

examples.en: The company succeeded in producing the key parts domestically.

examples.ko: 반도체 장비 국산화가 빠르게 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: Domestic production of semiconductor equipment is moving fast.

examples.ko: 국산화 비율을 높이려고 연구를 많이 해요.
examples.en: They do a lot of research to raise the rate of domestic production.
The government announced it will support domestic production of parts.
After production moved domestic, repairs became much easier.

examples.ko: 이 제품의 국산화는 거의 끝났다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that the move to domestic production of this product is almost done.

explain: 주로 기계, 부품, 기술처럼 수입하던 것을 우리나라에서 만들게 될 때 써요. 뉴스와 경제 이야기에서 '부품 국산화', '국산화 비율'처럼 자주 나와요. 반대로 외국에서 들여오는 것은 '수입'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이 기계는 부품 국산화율이 많이 높아졌어요.
phrases.en: The rate of domestic parts in this machine has risen a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전체 중 우리나라에서 만든 부분이 얼마인지 비율로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give the share of parts made domestically as a ratio.

phrases.en: The government is pushing for domestic production of key materials.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획을 세워 앞으로 이루려고 할 때 쓰는 뉴스 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news expression for planning to achieve something going forward.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 몇 년 만에 국산화를 이뤘어요.
phrases.en: That company achieved domestic production in a few years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표를 끝내 이루었다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense that the goal was finally accomplished.

explain_en: It is used when something that used to be imported, such as machines, parts or technology, comes to be made in Korea. You often see it in news and economy talk, as in '부품 국산화' or '국산화 비율'. The opposite idea is '수입' (import).

en: putting something on the market; releasing

examples.ko: 새 앨범 발매가 다음 달로 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: The new album's release was pushed to next month.
The line got long after news of the game console's release.
Everything sold out on the first day of sale.

examples.ko: 이 가수의 발매 기념 팬 행사가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a fan event for this singer's release.
Expectations were high even before release.

examples.ko: 한정판은 발매 후 며칠 안에 구해야 해요.
examples.en: The limited edition has to be bought within a few days of release.

explain: 음반·게임·상품이 처음 가게에 나와 팔리기 시작하는 것을 말해요. 책은 '출간', 영화는 '개봉', 앱이나 서비스는 '출시'라고 해서 대상에 따라 다른 단어를 써요. 앨범과 게임기에는 '발매'가 가장 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: When is the album's release date?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품이 처음 팔리는 날을 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common word for the day a product first goes on sale.

phrases.en: The new game console is scheduled for release next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 나오지 않았지만 곧 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something not yet out but coming soon.

phrases.en: That game went on sale yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품이 주어일 때 쓰는 동사 피동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive verb form, used when the product is the subject.

explain_en: It means a record, game or product first appears in stores and goes on sale. Korean picks different words by object: 출간 for books, 개봉 for movies, 출시 for apps and services. 발매 fits albums and game consoles best.

examples.en: I stock up on water and ramen in preparation for typhoons.
The government is stockpiling rice.
I stocked up on firewood in advance to get through the winter.
Keeping emergency food in stock gives me peace of mind.
I went to bed early today to save up my energy.
I'm worried because there isn't enough space to store supplies.

explain: 돈은 '저축하다', 물건이나 에너지는 '비축하다'로 구분해요. '힘을 비축하다'처럼 비유로도 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '쟁여 두다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Please keep a stock of emergency medicine at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 두다'를 붙여서 미리 모아서 놓아둔다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 두다 gives the sense of storing something in advance.

phrases.example: 라면을 미리 쟁여 둬서 걱정 없어요.
phrases.en: I stocked up on ramen in advance, so I'm not worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비축하다'를 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때 쓰는 입말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken version of 비축하다, used among friends.

phrases.example: 내일 시합을 위해 오늘은 힘을 비축해요.
phrases.en: I'm saving my strength today for tomorrow's match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 아니라 힘이나 체력을 아껴 두는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use, saving strength or energy rather than goods.

explain_en: Money is '저축하다', while goods and energy are '비축하다'. It can be used figuratively, as in '힘을 비축하다', and in casual talk people also say '쟁여 두다'.

en: to be repaid; to be redeemed

examples.ko: 대출금은 다음 달에 모두 상환될 거예요.
examples.en: The loan will be fully repaid next month.

examples.ko: 빌린 돈이 제때 상환되지 않아서 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: A problem came up because the borrowed money was not repaid on time.
When the principal is repaid, the interest also goes down.
Government bonds are repaid automatically when they mature.

examples.ko: 이 대출은 매달 조금씩 상환되고 있어요.
examples.en: This loan is being paid off a little each month.

examples.ko: 모든 빚이 상환된 날 가족이 함께 식사했어요.
examples.en: On the day all the debt was paid off, the family had a meal together.

explain: '상환하다'는 갚는 사람이 주어이고, '상환되다'는 빚이나 대출금이 주어일 때 써요. '대출금이 상환되다'처럼 돈이 갚아지는 결과를 말하고, 주로 금융 뉴스나 계약서에서 나와요.

phrases.en: The debt was repaid in full.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갚을 돈이 모두 갚아졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the whole amount owed has been paid back.

phrases.en: I pay interest until the loan is repaid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기한이나 조건을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to state a time limit or condition.

phrases.en: The loan repayment is all finished.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상환되다'보다 쉬운 말로, 갚는 일이 모두 끝났다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say 상환되다: the repayment is completely done.

explain_en: '상환하다' has the person who pays as its subject, while '상환되다' takes the debt or loan as its subject, as in '대출금이 상환되다'. It describes the result of money being paid back and appears mainly in financial news and contracts.

examples.en: This cargo will be loaded onto a ship at Busan Port tomorrow.
We loaded ten containers onto the ship.

examples.ko: 상품을 모두 선적하려면 이틀이 더 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes two more days to load all the goods.

examples.ko: 선적할 물건의 수량을 다시 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check the quantity of the goods to be shipped again.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 배에 짐을 선적하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, we couldn't load the cargo onto the ship.

examples.ko: 수출품을 선적한 뒤에 서류를 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll send you the documents after the exports are shipped.

explain: 무역이나 물류에서 짐을 배에 싣는 일을 말해요. 일상에서 짐을 차에 싣는 건 '싣다'라고 하고, '선적하다'는 배·수출 이야기에 써요. 반대로 짐을 내리는 것은 '하역하다'예요.

phrases.en: The cargo I ordered was loaded onto the ship today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐이 배에 실리는 일을 짐을 중심으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on the cargo being loaded onto a ship.
phrases.en_equiv: to be loaded onto a ship

phrases.en: Please tell me when the shipping date is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무역 서류나 메일에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in trade documents and emails.

phrases.en: I loaded the goods for export onto the ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선적하다'와 같은 뜻의 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say the same thing as 선적하다.

explain_en: It is used in trade and logistics for putting cargo onto a ship. For loading things into a car in daily life you say '싣다', so '선적하다' belongs to talk about ships and exports. The opposite, unloading cargo, is '하역하다'.

dis.h: load cargo onto a ship for shipping
gh: mount equipment onto a plane, ship, or computer

p.n: The other word is plain loading, without the shipping-trade sense.

t90.ax: We loaded ten containers onto the ship.
